title: How to play
intro:
**Horseless Carriage: How to play**

Two guided years against two rival car makers, Robin and Sam.

steps.welcome: You run a car company in the early days of the automobile. You're competing with Robin and Sam to build the cars people want to buy.
steps.goal: Money is the score. Every dollar you earn shows here, next to your name. When the clock runs out, the richest company wins.
steps.chain: Buyers want cars with certain specs. Specs come from stations in our factory. Stations come from research. So each year we research, then build, then sell.
steps.market: This is the market. Each square is a niche: a slice of the public with its own taste. The cars on it are buyers, waiting for a car they like. There are four today, all in the bottom-left corner.
steps.market-types: Every buyer today wants a plain car. In the full game some want trucks or sports cars, which pay more but need their own mainline. This first game is cars only.
steps.axes: What does a buyer want? Read the axes. Today the public cares about two things: safety along the bottom, and reliability up the side. The further a niche is from the bottom-left, the more of each it wants.
steps.axes-why: The buyers in the bottom-left don't ask for much. Three of them want nothing at all: any car will do. This one wants one reliability, the one box beside its row. That is why we start down here. The niche in the top-right wants three of each, and nobody can build that car yet. Whoever can will earn the most.
steps.tracks: These are the research tracks: five things a car can be good at. Only two of them are on the market at a time, the two along its edges. The other three wait here until they come into fashion.
steps.tracks-slots: Each track has six slots, and each slot shows a station. Once your marker reaches a slot, you can build that station in your factory. That's all research does: it lets you build things.
steps.tracks-markers: This is your marker on each track. The blue ones are Robin's and the purple ones are Sam's. On the two tracks on the market, everyone starts on the first slot: the brake and the battery are common knowledge, and anyone can build them. On the three tracks off the board, everyone starts at the start spot, knowing nothing.
steps.office: The planning office sets the order of play, and the order matters. The first to build gets first pick from the supply. The first to sell gets the best buyer.
steps.factory: And this is your factory. You can build on any black square. The loading bay in the corner isn't floor: everything you build has to connect to it, each tile touching the next, so the cars can get out.
steps.departments: You start with two departments on your floor. The research department gives you one research step a year. The planning department earns you one Gantt chart a year, and Gantt charts decide who picks first. Each one only needs to touch the bay, or a tile that does.
steps.supply: Stations, mainlines and departments all come from this shared supply, and it's limited. Once the radiators are gone, nobody can build one.
steps.cards: These are your market cards. Each one brings new buyers to the part of the market you choose. You play one at the end of each year.
steps.place-departments: Your two departments start next to the loading bay. In a real game you can drag them anywhere, as long as each one touches the bay or the other department. Today, leave them where they are, so the floor stays clear for your first car. Tap Done.
steps.others-setup: Robin and Sam start the same way, with the same floor and the same two departments.
steps.research: Each year starts with research. Because it comes first, anything you research you can build and sell later the same year. Your research department gives you one step.
steps.research-rules: A step moves one marker forward one slot. It can be any marker on any track, even Robin's or Sam's. Why help a rival? Because the player in the first engineering slot can build anything someone else has researched: patents. I'll show you how when we set the focus. More research departments give you more steps, but you can't move the same marker twice in one year. Another player still can.
steps.research-capacity: Or you can spend the step on your assembly capacity: how many cars each mainline builds a year. More cars means more money. But a car nobody wants won't sell, so this year we'll research.
steps.research-clock: Some slots show a punch clock. When a marker reaches one, the timecard moves down a step. The more research gets done, the sooner the game ends.
steps.research-space: Let's research reliability. Your marker is on the battery, and the next slot is the chassis: a big, simple station that gives a car one reliability. Tap the battery, where your marker is.
steps.research-marker: There are three markers on the battery. Tap yours, the red one.
steps.research-done: Your marker is on the chassis now. You can build a chassis and point a reliability indicator at it. Each research step unlocks one station.
steps.others-research-robin: Robin moves up the safety track, to the brake. Safety is the other track on the market, so a brake helps sell cars right now.
steps.others-research-sam: Sam moves up the design track, which is off the board, to the paint shop. No buyer cares about design yet, so why bother? At the end of each year, one track leaves the market, and the off-board track with the most research replaces it. Sam is betting on design. Keep that in mind.
steps.focus: Now we set the focus: the order of play for the year. The focus track runs from engineering on the left to sales on the right. Slot 1 builds first and gets the patents. The last open slot sells first. With three players, slots 4 and 5 are closed.
steps.focus-patents: Your slot also decides what you can copy. Slot 1 can build any station that someone else has researched. Slot 2 can build only what both other players have researched. Slot 3 can build only from its own research. And when the supply runs short, slot 1 is served first, then slot 2.
steps.focus-gantt: Who picks first? Whoever has the most Gantt charts. Taking a slot spends all your Gantt charts and puts you back to zero. If you pass, you keep them and get whichever slot is left. A chart you save this year gets you a better pick next year.
steps.focus-do: You have the most Gantt charts, so you pick first. Take slot 1. We want to reach the supply before Robin and Sam, and slot 1 gets the patents.
steps.others-focus-robin: Robin takes slot 3, at the sales end. There are four buyers and three companies, and Robin wants first pick.
steps.others-focus-sam: Sam passes and keeps the Gantt charts. That leaves slot 2 for Sam. Next year Sam will have the most charts and pick first.
steps.build: Now everyone builds at once, each in their own factory. The Add gallery holds everything you can build this year. Tap a piece, and it appears on your floor for you to drag into place.
steps.build-rules: Every tile follows three rules. It must sit on black floor, not on the loading bay. It can't overlap another tile. And it must touch the bay, or a tile that does. Anything breaking a rule is outlined in pink until you fix it.
steps.add-mainline: Every factory needs a production line, called a mainline. You can't build cars without one. Tap the car mainline in the Add gallery.
steps.place-mainline: Drag the mainline to the ringed spot, beside the loading bay.
steps.mainline: Look at its four sides, marked A, B, C and D: the four steps of building a car. A is the structure. B is the drive. C is the factory options. D is the extras. Each station belongs to one step, and goes against that side.
steps.add-dealer: Cars need someone to sell them, so you need a dealer. Add your small dealership.
steps.rotate-dealer: Tap Rotate to turn it on its side, so it fits next to the mainline.
steps.place-dealer: Now drag it against the mainline's left side. A dealer sells the cars from the mainline it touches, so every dealer has to touch a mainline, and every mainline needs a dealer.
steps.dealer-done: The mainline and the dealer are touching, so this dealer sells whatever this mainline builds. Right now that's a car with no specs at all, and the bottom-left buyers would still take it. But people will soon want more.
steps.zones: Now for a station. The chassis is an A station, so it goes against the A side. See the hatching? Each step has its own pattern, and a station, its indicators and the matching side of the mainline together make one manufacturing zone.
steps.zones-rule: One rule about zones: a zone can't have two of the same station. One chassis per zone, one brake per zone. If you want two chassis, put them on different sides or different mainlines.
steps.place-chassis: Drag it below the mainline, against the A side.
steps.add-spec: A station does nothing on its own. It needs a spec indicator pointing at it, to show you know how to build it well. Your reliability research lets you put one reliability indicator on the chassis. Tap Add spec.
steps.place-spec: The indicator appears on a free square touching the chassis. Drag it to the ringed square, on the chassis's left, next to the mainline. That keeps the right side free for next year. It could go on any square touching the chassis, as long as it stays in the chassis's zone.
steps.spec-done: That's a spec. Every car from this mainline now has one reliability, because there's one reliability indicator in its zones. Two indicators would mean two reliability. That's how a car gets its numbers.
steps.paint-why: Let's add one more station, one that only slot 1 lets us build. Slot 1 can build anything another player has researched, and Sam's marker is on paint, the first slot of design. Design is not on the market yet, so paint earns nothing this year. But Sam is betting design will come, and next year we may not have slot 1. So let's build it while we can.
steps.move-dealer: Paint is a C station, so it goes against side C, on the left, where the dealer is. You can still move anything you placed this year, so drag the dealer down to the ringed spot. It still touches the mainline by one square, and that's enough.
steps.rotate-paint: Rotate it so it lies flat.
steps.place-paint: Drag it against the mainline's left side, above the dealer.
steps.paint-spec: Its spec is design. You never researched design, but from slot 1 you can use Sam's research for the indicator too. Tap Add spec.
steps.place-paint-spec: Drag the indicator to the ringed square, above the paint.
steps.paint-done: Every car from this mainline now has one design as well. It's worth nothing until design reaches the market, but Sam thinks it will.
steps.marketing-why: Last, the dealer. A dealer sells through a market window: a frame it places on the market, and it sells to one niche inside the frame. On its own, a small dealer's window covers two niches. A marketing department next to it makes the window two by two: more niches, and more buyers to choose from.
steps.place-marketing: And drag it below the dealer. Marketing has to touch the dealer it works for.
steps.expansion: One last thing, and it's free. Each year you add a floor expansion: more black floor for next year. It comes with its own loading bay, and the strip next to that bay has to stay clear, so the door can open. You can't build on it until next year.
steps.done-build: Nothing is outlined in pink, so everything is legal. Tap Done.
steps.others-build: Robin and Sam build too. When two of us want the same piece, the supply goes in engineering order: you, then Sam, then Robin.
steps.others-build-look: Look at what Robin built. Robin added three new stations, each with its own spec indicator: a brake and a window pane for safety, and a battery for reliability.
steps.others-build-robin-specs: Each indicator adds one point of spec. That's two for safety and one for reliability, so Robin's cars have two safety and one reliability. That reaches buyers further along the safety axis than yours can.
steps.others-build-sam: Sam built a brake and a battery, for one safety and one reliability. Sam also added a second research department.
steps.others-build-research: So did Robin. Each research department gives one research step a year, so from next year Robin and Sam each get two steps, and you still get one.
steps.brochures: Now every company prints its sales brochures, which tell buyers what each dealer can sell this year. Nobody makes any choices here; it all follows from the factories. First, planning: each planning department adds one Gantt chart. Reaching ten on the track punches the clock.
steps.brochures-specs: Then every dealer shows what it can sell. Its specs come from the indicators in its mainline's zones: yours shows one reliability, no safety, and one design, which no buyer wants yet. Its window is two by two, thanks to the marketing department next to it.
steps.brochures-reach: The faint rectangle on the market shows every niche your dealer could reach this year: the ones that want no more than one reliability and no safety.
steps.sell: Then we sell, and here the order matters. Selling starts at the right of the focus track: slot 3 first, then slot 2, then slot 1. On your turn you must sell if you can, from one dealer, into one niche.
steps.sell-price: What is a buyer worth? It depends on where they are. The shading cuts the market into four price segments: the cheapest at the bottom-left, then the second band, then the third band, and the most expensive at the top-right. Each segment's price marker shows what its buyers pay.
steps.sell-price-why: Only the bottom-left segment has buyers today, so it gets the six dollar marker: the best price always goes to the most expensive segment that has buyers. Once there are buyers higher up, this corner's price will drop. The easy buyers are easy money, but only while nobody else wants them.
steps.sell-window-rule: A window can only cover niches your dealer can satisfy: nothing inside it can want more than your specs. It can hang off the edge of the board, and it can overlap another window. Once you place it, it stays for the year.
steps.others-sell-robin: Robin sells first, from the sales end of the focus track. Robin's window goes down, and Robin sells one car from it, for six dollars.
steps.others-sell-sam: Then Sam places a window and sells one car too. That leaves two buyers.
steps.sell-window: Your turn. Drag your dealer's window onto the ringed spot. It covers the last two buyers, and they want nothing special, so you can sell to them. Then confirm.
steps.sell-niche: There are two buyers inside your window, in two niches. Your mainline builds one car a year, so you can sell one. Pick either niche.
steps.sold: Six dollars, next to your name. That was your whole capacity for the year: one mainline, one car. Selling goes in rounds until nobody can sell any more, and you can't pass while you still can sell. Robin and Sam are out of cars too, so selling is over.
steps.finish: Is the game over? Not yet. The timecard decides: when it reaches the last space on the punch clock, it flips over, and the game ends after that year. If the clock never runs out, the game ends after the seventh year, when all the floor expansions are used up.
steps.expectations: Now the public changes its mind. The black arrow has pointed at safety all year, and now safety leaves the market. It goes under the off-board tracks, and its axis comes off the board.
steps.expectations-min: But safety still matters. Its minimum specification goes up to one, as this marker beside the market shows. From now on, no car sells without at least one safety. Robin and Sam built brakes last year. Your dealer has none. Remember that.
steps.expectations-new: Which track takes its place? The off-board track whose research has gone furthest past its innovation marker. Sam's design step is the only research off the board, so design comes onto the market, and Sam is already a step ahead on it. Your paint is ready for it too.
steps.expectations-arrow: The arrow now points at reliability: next year reliability leaves the market, and its minimum goes up. Plan for it.
steps.grow: Last, demand grows. Each of us plays a market card face down beside a quadrant of the market. The market is split into four quadrants: one at the bottom-left, two at the bottom-right, three at the top-left and four at the top-right.
steps.grow-neutral: These black cards were played first, face down, from the neutral deck. They belong to nobody, and in each quadrant they're turned over last.
steps.grow-cards: Here is your hand. Every card is a map of one quadrant of the market. Each car on it is a spark: a niche in that quadrant where people are warming to cars.
steps.grow-sparks: A spark brings a new buyer to its niche every year. So play a card where your dealer can reach, and next year the buyers will be waiting for you.
steps.grow-clocks: Some cards also punch the clock. Each clock on a card moves the timecard down one step, bringing the end of the game closer.
steps.grow-year: The number in a card's bottom corner is its year. This one says three, so you can play it once you've placed three floor expansions. You've placed one, so today you can play only your year one cards. Bigger factories unlock bigger cards.
steps.play-card: Play this card. It has one car spark and one punch clock.
steps.play-quadrant: Put it beside quadrant one, where your dealer can reach.
steps.others-cards: Sam and Robin play theirs face down. Nobody knows where the others' sparks will land until the cards are turned over.
steps.reveal-sparks: The cards are turned over one quadrant at a time, with the black ones last. Each spark flies off its card onto its niche and stays there for good, and each punch clock on a card moves the timecard down.
steps.reveal-buyers: Each spark brings one new buyer, up to two buyers per spark. There they are.
steps.reveal-neutral: Then the black cards. They have no sparks: each one puts a single buyer straight onto the niche it shows.
steps.reveal-prices: Then the prices are reset: the segment closest to the top-right with buyers gets the six dollar marker, the next one gets the four, and so on down.
steps.year-two: That was a whole year. The second year works the same way, and this time you'll do more of it yourself. Look at your dealer: safety now has a minimum of one, and your dealer has none. It can't sell anything until you build a brake.
steps.year-two-why: We could have built one last year. Anyone can: the brake is the first slot of the safety track, where every marker started. We spent last year on the chassis and the paint instead, so now we have to build a brake this year. Every station is a choice.
steps.y2-research: Research comes first, as always. Your marker is on the chassis, and one more step gets you the car body: a second reliability indicator, for two reliability. Why two? Look at the market. Two buyers are waiting together in the second segment, at six dollars each, and they want two reliability and no design. Nobody else can reach them today. Tap the chassis, where your marker is.
steps.y2-research-done: Your marker is on the car body now. The punch clocks are on slots four and six, so not this year.
steps.y2-others-research-sam: Sam researches before Robin this year, because the order follows last year's engineering order: you, then Sam, then Robin. Sam has two research departments now, so two steps. The first goes to design again, up to the windscreen: design is on the market now, and Sam's bet is paying off. The second step raises Sam's assembly capacity to two, so each of Sam's mainlines now builds two cars a year.
steps.y2-others-research-robin: Robin also takes two steps. The first goes off the board, to range: a bet on the next track to come in. The second raises Robin's capacity to two as well. Two steps, two different markers: nobody can move the same marker twice in a year, though another player still can.
steps.y2-focus: Now the focus. Sam kept a Gantt chart last year and earned another, so Sam has two. You and Robin have one each. Sam picks first.
steps.y2-others-focus-sam: Sam takes slot 1. Why? Patents. Slot 1 can build anything another player has researched, like your chassis or Robin's window pane. Sam's company has nothing new to build, but it can copy everyone else's.
steps.y2-focus-do: Now you. You and Robin are tied on charts, and a tie goes to whoever had the better engineering slot last year: you. Take slot 3, the sales end, so you sell first this year, before Robin and Sam get to the buyers.
steps.y2-others-focus-robin: Robin takes slot 2, the only one left. Passing would have given Robin the same slot and kept the chart. From slot 2, Robin can copy only what both you and Sam have researched.
steps.y2-build: Time to build. The expansion you placed last year is floor now, and you can build on it as long as its keep-clear strip stays empty. Everything from last year is fixed in place. Two stations today: the brake and the car body.
steps.y2-add-brake: First the brake. It's a B station, so it goes on the mainline's B side, on the right. Add the brake.
steps.y2-place-brake: Drag it against the right side of the mainline, below the loading bay.
steps.y2-brake-spec: It needs a spec indicator. Your safety marker has been on the brake slot since the start, so you can add a safety indicator. Tap Add spec.
steps.y2-place-brake-spec: Drag the indicator to the ringed square, touching the brake. It's a B indicator, so it joins the brake's zone, along with the mainline's B side.
steps.y2-add-carbody: Now the car body, an A station. It has to join an A zone, but it doesn't need to touch the mainline: a station touching another station of the same step joins that station's zone, and the chassis's zone already reaches the mainline. Add the car body.
steps.y2-place-carbody: Drag it next to the chassis, onto the ringed spot.
steps.y2-carbody-spec: And its indicator, from the car body slot you just reached. Tap Add spec.
steps.y2-place-carbody-spec: Drag it to the ringed square, touching the car body.
steps.y2-spec-done: Count the indicators in the mainline's zones: two reliability, one safety and one design. Every car from this line now has two reliability, one safety and one design. Your dealer meets the minimum again, and it can sell higher up the board than anyone else.
steps.y2-second-why: One more thing, and it's the big one. Two buyers are waiting at six dollars, but your mainline builds one car a year. A second mainline touching your dealer gives it two cars to sell, and last year's expansion has room for one.
steps.y2-rotate-mainline: Tap Rotate twice, until its C side faces right.
steps.y2-place-mainline: Drag it onto the expansion, to the ringed spot, with its C side against the paint and its corner touching the dealer.
steps.y2-shared-dealer: Now your dealer touches two mainlines. For each spec, a dealer shows the lower of its two mainlines. This new line has no stations yet, so look at the dealer's cubes: reliability and safety now read zero. A second line on the same dealer needs the same specs as the first, or it drags the dealer down.
steps.y2-shared-zones: But design still reads one. Two lines can share stations: a zone that touches both mainlines counts for both. The paint sits between them, against both C sides, so the new line already has one design. And we couldn't build paint today: from slot 3 we can only build what we researched ourselves. Taking slot 1 last year is paying off.
steps.y2-add-chassis: Reliability first, on the A side, at the top. A second chassis is allowed: you can build the same station twice, as long as each one is in a different zone. Add the chassis.
steps.y2-rotate-chassis: Rotate it once, so it lies along the top.
steps.y2-place-chassis: Drag it against the mainline's top side.
steps.y2-chassis-spec: Then its reliability indicator. Tap Add spec.
steps.y2-place-chassis-spec: Drag the indicator to the ringed square, next to the chassis.
steps.y2-add-brake2: Then safety, on the B side, the left. Add the brake.
steps.y2-place-brake2: Drag it next to the mainline, onto the ringed spot.
steps.y2-place-brake2-spec: Drag the indicator to the ringed square, next to the brake.
steps.y2-battery-why: Last, a second point of reliability, from a battery on the C side. The C side is the paint's zone, and it touches both lines, so a battery there counts for both. It doesn't have to touch the paint; it can sit further back. A zone runs through indicators as well as stations, so a battery behind the paint's indicator joins the zone.
steps.y2-place-battery: Drag it to the ringed spot, behind the paint's indicator.
steps.y2-place-battery-spec: Drag the indicator to the ringed square, between the battery and the paint.
steps.y2-second-done: Count again. The new line has two reliability, from its chassis and the battery, plus one safety and the paint's design. The battery counts for the first line too, which now has three reliability. Your dealer shows the lower of the two, so its cubes are back, and now it has two cars a year to sell.
steps.y2-done-build: This year's expansion is already placed where it fits. You can drag it anywhere it touches the factory along the grid, as long as it covers no keep-clear strip and leaves its own strip free. It's fine where it is. Tap Done.
steps.y2-others-build: Robin and Sam build. This year Sam builds first, from slot 1, then Robin, then you. That only matters when the supply runs short, and today it doesn't.
steps.y2-others-build-look: Look at Robin's factory. There's a second mainline out on last year's expansion, with its own dealer, brake and battery. Two mainlines at capacity two make four cars a year.
steps.y2-others-build-sam: Sam did the same, with a second mainline and dealer. Sam also added a windscreen and a paint shop, for two design, which reaches the right half of the board.
steps.y2-others-build-yours: But nobody else has two reliability, so the two buyers at six dollars are all yours.
steps.y2-brochures: Now the brochures. Each planning department adds one Gantt chart. Your dealer now shows two reliability, one safety and one design, with a medium window. Look at Robin's first dealer: it had two safety last year and has one now, because it touches two mainlines, and a dealer shows the lower of their specs. See how much further up the market you can reach now.
steps.y2-sell-window: You sell first this year. Drag the window to the ringed spot, two rows higher than last year. The two buyers at the top of it want two reliability and no design, and you have that. With only one niche to sell into, the sale happens as soon as you confirm.
steps.y2-sold: Twelve dollars: both buyers at six, one car from each mainline, through one dealer. That's what a second mainline is for. The other way to sell more is the capacity track: each step on it adds one car a year to every mainline you own.
steps.y2-others-sell-robin: Robin sells next, in the bottom-left corner: two buyers in one niche, and capacity two, so two cars at once. Eight dollars, four each. Buyers showed up higher on the board, so the corner's price fell, as I warned you.
steps.y2-others-sell-sam: Sam reaches across the board: two design opens up the columns on the right, and the buyer there pays six.
steps.y2-sell-rounds: Another round, in the same order. You have no cars left. Robin's dealer sells again, one more car in the corner, for four: a dealer keeps selling from its window each round until its mainlines run out of cars. Sam's second dealer can't reach any buyer, so selling is over, and the windows come off the board. With two dealers of your own, you could sell from either, and where both windows cover a niche, you choose which dealer sells.
steps.y2-finish: The timecard is still far from the end of the clock, so the game goes on.
steps.y2-expectations: The public changes its mind again. Reliability leaves the market, and its minimum becomes one. You have two; Robin and Sam have one each, just enough. Everyone can still sell this time.
steps.y2-expectations-tie: Which track comes in? Range and safety are tied: Robin is one step past the innovation marker on each. A tie goes to the track that's higher in the off-board stack, and range is on top.
steps.y2-expectations-new: Robin's bet paid off, and Robin starts the new track one step ahead of everyone. The arrow turns to design: next year design leaves, and its minimum will be one. Only Sam and you have any: your paint, from slot 1.
steps.y2-others-cards: Demand grows, and the cards go down in engineering order: Sam, then Robin, then you. They're played face down, so you won't know where their sparks land until the cards are turned over.
steps.y2-grow: Your turn. You have two floor expansions now, so you can play a year two card. Play this one: two sparks and two punch clocks. Two sparks is two new buyers a year, every year, where you can reach them.
steps.y2-play-quadrant: Put it beside quadrant one again: your dealer can reach its left half.
steps.y2-reveal: The cards are turned over, and the sparks land: two from your card, two from Robin's next to yours, and two from Sam's in quadrant two. The clock punches twice for your card, and twice for Robin's.
steps.y2-reveal-buyers: Then the buyers arrive: one per spark, up to two per spark on a niche. That's nine new buyers this year.
steps.y2-reveal-neutral: Then the three black cards bring three more buyers.
steps.y2-reveal-prices: Then the prices. The second segment keeps the six, and the corner keeps the four, because both still have buyers.
steps.year-three: After two years, you know every rule in the game. The rest is judgement. Research what the market will want next year, not this year. Build a second mainline or raise your capacity as soon as you have more buyers than cars. Take slot 1 when the supply is short or you want to copy someone else's research, and take the sales end when buyers are scarce. And save a Gantt chart when passing costs you nothing.
steps.game-end: The game ends after the year the timecard flips, or after year seven. Then the richest company wins. If two are tied, the one with the higher sales focus wins.
steps.full-game: We played the introductory rules. In the full game, trucks and sports cars come to market too: a truck pays one dollar more and a sports car two, but each needs its own, bigger mainline. Those stayed in the box today.
steps.finish-tutorial: The company is yours. Build boldly and sell hard. If I can dream it, you can do it!

hints.place-departments: Tap Done in the bar below.
hints.research-space: Tap the highlighted space on the reliability track.
hints.research-marker: Tap your red marker in the gallery.
hints.focus-do: Tap slot 1 on the focus track.
hints.add-mainline: Tap Add in the bar below, then the car mainline.
hints.place-mainline: Drag the mainline onto the ringed spot.
hints.add-dealer: Tap Add, then the small dealership.
hints.place-dealer: Drag the dealer onto the ringed spot.
hints.place-chassis: Drag the chassis onto the ringed spot.
hints.place-spec: Drag the indicator onto the ringed square.
hints.move-dealer: Drag the dealer onto the ringed spot.
hints.place-paint: Drag the paint onto the ringed spot.
hints.place-paint-spec: Drag the indicator onto the ringed square.
hints.add-marketing: Tap Add, then the marketing department.
hints.place-marketing: Drag it onto the ringed spot.
hints.sell-window: Drag the window above the board onto the ringed spot, then tap Confirm.
hints.sell-niche: Tap one of the highlighted niches inside your window.
hints.play-quadrant: Tap the ringed space beside quadrant one.
hints.y2-research: Tap the chassis slot on the reliability track.
hints.y2-focus-do: Tap slot 3 on the focus track.
hints.y2-place-brake: Drag the brake onto the ringed spot.
hints.y2-place-brake-spec: Drag the indicator onto the ringed square.
hints.y2-add-carbody: Tap Add, then the car body.
hints.y2-place-carbody: Drag the car body onto the ringed spot.
hints.y2-place-carbody-spec: Drag the indicator onto the ringed square.
hints.y2-sell-window: Drag the window above the board onto the ringed spot, then tap Confirm.
hints.y2-play-quadrant: Tap the ringed space beside quadrant one.
hints.y2-add-mainline: Tap Add, then the car mainline.
hints.y2-rotate-mainline: Tap Rotate until the C side faces right.
hints.y2-place-mainline: Drag the mainline onto the ringed spot.
hints.y2-place-chassis: Drag the chassis onto the ringed spot.
hints.y2-place-chassis-spec: Drag the indicator onto the ringed square.
hints.y2-place-brake2: Drag the brake onto the ringed spot.
hints.y2-place-brake2-spec: Drag the indicator onto the ringed square.
hints.y2-place-battery: Drag the battery onto the ringed spot.
hints.y2-place-battery-spec: Drag the indicator onto the ringed square.
